subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals for ZenHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals for ZenHealth

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to confirm next steps. Tell me if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- Lack of model-level observability: limited dashboards for prompt-level throughput/latency and error breakdowns.
- No automated regression detection for output quality across releases (we heard false positives from recent model swap).
- Hard to correlate user incidents to inference traces and upstream logs.

Current stack:
- In-house UI service + Postgres for user data
- Using a hosted LLM endpoint today (vendor X) for generation and embedding workflows
- Basic Datadog for infra metrics; no end-to-end tracing tied to model requests

Success criteria for your evaluation:
- Dashboarding: per-route/per-model dashboards showing token-level cost, 95/99 latency, and error rates
- Tracing hooks: request-level trace ids that link to your frontend session and backend jobs
- Evals: setup golden prompt sets + automated regression alerts (precision/recall/acceptance-rate) with daily reports
- Rollout guardrails: canary policies + automatic fallback to previous model variant if evals drop below threshold

Proposed scope and timeline:
1) Share our "Observability playbook" + golden prompts (attached) — today
2) 2-week eval window: we’ll provide a pre-configured dashboard and tracing hooks; you run golden prompts on your sample dataset
3) Weekly sync (30 min) to review metrics and any regressions; decision point at end of week 2 for pilot expansion

Open questions for your team:
- Which routes (endpoints) should we instrument first? You mentioned the patient-summary generator and discharge note assistant — confirm these two.
- Any NDA / security checklist items on our side we should surface before we send a small data sample?

Attachments: redwood-observability-playbook.pdf (playbook + dashboard screenshots), golden-prompts-v1.csv (seed prompt set)

Thanks — I’ll put together the dashboard links and a short config guide.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Alex Johnson <alex@zenhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Observability & evals for ZenHealth

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. This is great and captures our needs. A few clarifications:

- Confirming priority routes: patient-summary generator, discharge-note assistant, and one ad-hoc triage flow (we’ll pick the triage endpoint by Friday).
- We want the evals to include a small human-in-loop check: our clinical reviewer will grade a sample of 200 prompts for clinical accuracy and hallucination rate.
- Security: we do need the SOC 2 details and a brief on how you handle PHI during the eval window (even anonymized).

Next steps from our side:
- I’ll loop in procurement once we confirm the pilot scope (expect that Friday).
- Clinical reviewer: I’ll introduce Dr. Patel (cc’d in follow-up) to the eval plan next week.

Looking forward to the dashboard — can you also include a cost projection for the 2-week eval based on our estimated throughput (~50k tokens/day)?

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of ML Ops | ZenHealth
alex@zenhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Observability & evals for ZenHealth

Alex —

Great — thanks for the confirmations. Quick replies inline: 

- Priority routes: patient-summary generator, discharge-note assistant, plus triage flow (will await final route name on Friday).
- Human-in-loop: totally — we’ll integrate a small review UI and include the 200-sample pass-through in the eval. We’ll add a field for reviewer grade so we can surface clinical-accuracy metrics on the dashboard.
- SOC 2 / PHI during eval: attaching our SOC 2 summary in the playbook; for the eval window we recommend pseudonymizing PHI fields and we’ll provide an encrypted upload link. Marcus — can you confirm the data ingestion options we should send to Alex (S3 signed URL vs secure sync)?

Cost projection for 2-week eval (approx):
- Estimated tokens: 50k tokens/day x 14 = 700k tokens
- Cost: ~$0.063 per 1k tokens (pilot pricing) => estimate: $44.10 (compute-only; excludes storage/optional human-review fees)

Next steps (owner):
- Marissa: share dashboard links + access to playbook (today) — DONE (attachments)
- Alex: confirm triage route by Friday (2/27) — Alex
- Marcus: provide secure ingest options and minimal config for tracing hooks (today) — Marcus
- ZenHealth: confirm clinical reviewer and procurement timeline (by Friday) — Alex/Procurement

Thanks — I’ll follow up with dashboard links in the next hour.

Best,
Marissa

Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Observability & evals for ZenHealth

Alex / Marissa —

Quick note on ingest + tracing hooks:
- We can provide both ingestion options: S3 signed URL (recommended for one-off uploads) and a secure sync agent for ongoing flows. I’ll include minimal example code in the Confluence page.
- Tracing hooks: we’ll add a request_id header to the instrumented client; Redwood will return a trace_id in the response headers that links to the dashboard and spans. That trace_id will surface in logs and Sentry traces if you opt into integration.
- Data handling: for the pilot, pseudonymization is fine; we’ll store only the minimal request metadata and truncated tokens needed for debugging (per our data retention policy).

I’ll drop the example config + small ingest playbook to the shared link (Marcus) and follow up if you want a short tech sync.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
